mental filtering: This thinking styles involves a 'filtering in' and 'filtering out' process - a sort of 'tunnel vision,' focusing on only one part of a situation and ignoring the rest. Usually this means looking at the negative parts of a situation and forgetting the positive parts.
jumping to conclusions: fortune-telling: We jump to conclusions when we assume that we know what someone else is thinking.
jumping to conclusions: mind-reading: We jump to conclusions when we assume that we know what is going to happen in the future.
personalization: This involves blaming yourself for everything that goes wrong or could go wrong, even when you may only be partly responsible or not responsible at all. You might be taking 100% responsibility for the occurrence of external events.
catastrophizing: Catastrophising occurs when we 'blow things out of proportion', and we view the situation as terrible, awful, dreadful, and horrible, even though the reality is that the problem itself is quite small.
black-and-white or polarized thinking /: This thinking style involves seeing only one extreme or the other. You are either wrong or right, good or bad and so on. There are no in-betweens or shades of gray.
should statements: Sometimes by saying 'I should...' or 'I must...' you can put unreasonable demands or pressure on yourself and others. Although these statements are not always unhelpful, they can sometimes create unrealistic expectations.
overgeneralization: When we overgeneralise, we take one instance in the past or present, and impose it on all current or future situations. If we say 'You always...' or 'Everyone...', or 'I never...' then we are probably overgeneralising.
labeling and mislabeling: We label ourselves and others when we make global statements based on behaviour in specific situations. We might use this label even though there are many more examples that aren't consistent with that label.
discounting the positive: In this thinking style, you magnify the positive attributes of other people and minimise your own positive attributes. It's as though you're explaining away your own positive characteristics.
